deal_stage: Technical discovery completed, proposal in progress
pitch_summary: Multi-agent Gen AI platform to triage and resolve transaction disputes and chargebacks, absorbing the growing complaint volume driven by international expansion (US, Middle East) without multiplying risk-operations headcount.
proposed_solution: Agentic pipeline hosted on Azure with dispute-classification agents, evidence cross-referencing (statement, geolocation, behavioral pattern), and automatic resolution of low-complexity cases, with a human in the loop for high-value cases. 16-week implementation, US$850k in Year 1 (license + services).

ceo: David Vélez is founder and CEO of Nu Holdings/Nubank, holding roughly 75% of voting power via super-voting shares
In February 2026, Bloomberg reported Vélez working to expand Nubank's global base to more than 127 million customers, including nearly 60% of Brazil's adult population
Nubank's return on equity (ROE) in the most recent quarter cited by Bloomberg was 31%, versus 23.3% for Itaú Unibanco

Vélez confirmed that the conditional approval for a national US banking license (obtained in January 2026) — internally called 'Act Three' — is a long-term goal, while the stated focus remains Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia
In April 2026, Nubank formalized its entry into the Middle East, headquartered in Abu Dhabi in partnership with Wio Bank, targeting expansion into Asia and MENA

The company operates with 131 million customers, US$78 billion in assets, and US$2.82 billion in net income in 2025, and is among the four finalists to acquire Banco Caixa Geral Brasil and obtain a full domestic banking license

Given this track record of aggressive multi-geography expansion under concentrated shareholder control, Vélez tends to evaluate any automation proposal through the lens of 'does this free up operational capacity to sustain the pace of international expansion without compromising the capital efficiency that today outperforms traditional banks?'
